name: Nepal
native: संघीय लोकतान्त्रिक गणतन्त्र नेपाल (Saṅghīya Lokatāntrika Gaṇatantra Nepāla)

predecessors.name: Gorkha Kingdom
predecessors.text: Gorkha and the hill lands Prithvi Narayan Shah had annexed between 1744 and 1768 (Nuwakot, Dolakha, Makwanpur and the Kathmandu Valley rim)

predecessors.name: Kathmandu (Kantipur)
predecessors.text: the city-states of Kathmandu, Lalitpur and Bhaktapur, taken 1768-1769, 'completing his conquest of the Nepal Valley'

ledger.x: 25 September 1768: Prithvi Narayan Shah proclaims the Kingdom of Nepal.
1768: the capital moves from Gorkha to Kathmandu.
1771: Kaski and the Sapta Gandaki region annexed.
ledger.cp: Kaski and the Sapta Gandaki principalities

ledger.x: 1774: the Kirant country to the Tista.
1806: the hill country to the Sutlej.
ledger.cp: Sirmur, Bushahr and the other hill chiefdoms between Garhwal and the Sutlej

ledger.x: 24 August 1809: the Gorkhas return to the Sutlej.
October 1814: the Anglo-Nepalese War opens in the west.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 27 April 1815: Almora falls and Kumaon is lost.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 15 May 1815: Malaun and the Far West.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 15 May 1815: the western fighting ends with the surrender at Malaun; the war continued on other fronts until the treaty was ratified on 4 March 1816.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 4 March 1816: the Treaty of Sugauli takes the western Terai.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 4 March 1816: the Mechi becomes the eastern border.

ledger.x: 1846: the Rana prime ministers take power.
3 April 1855: the Nepalese army enters Tibet.
24 March 1856: the Treaty of Thapathali ends the occupation.
28 May 2008: the Kingdom becomes a Federal Democratic Republic.

wars.name: Unification of Nepal
wars.outcome: Gorkha annexes the Kathmandu Valley (1768-1769), Kaski (1771), Lamjung and Tanahun (1782), the east to the Tista (1774), Bheri (1786), Jumla (1789), Doti (1790) and Kumaon (1791).

wars.name: Sino-Nepalese War
wars.outcome: Stalemate: Nepal returned its 1788 conquests in the Treaty of Kerung (1789) and, after the Qing army reached Nuwakot, concluded the Treaty of Betrawati on 2 October 1792 ('Status quo antebellum'); Nepal accepted Qing suzerainty over Tibet and sent tribute…

wars.name: Gorkha conquest of Kumaon
wars.outcome: Kumaon annexed; Gorkha rule lasted 24 years ('cruel and oppressive' in a number of texts).

wars.name: Gorkha conquest of Garhwal
wars.outcome: Garhwal annexed; the royal family went into exile and the Gorkhas ruled the region for twelve years.

wars.name: Gorkha siege of Kangra
wars.outcome: The Gorkha army withdrew to the Sutlej by agreement on 24 August 1809, 'helpless against the superior Westernized Sikh forces'.

wars.name: Anglo-Nepalese War
wars.outcome: British victory: Nepal lost about one third of its land at the Treaty of Sugauli (ratified 4 March 1816): Kumaon, Garhwal and the hills west of the Mahakali, the Kali-Rapti Terai, the Mechi-Teesta strip and Sikkim; it kept its independence and accepted a…

wars.name: Nepal-Tibet War
wars.outcome: Nepalese victory on the page's infobox: Tibet agreed in the Treaty of Thapathali (24 March 1856) to pay Nepal 10,000 rupees a year and to admit a Nepalese agency at Lhasa; 'Nepalese territorial ambitions were dropped'.

certainty.note: Hill and Himalayan frontiers with Tibet, Sikkim, Garhwal and the western hill states are approximate; the Treaty of Betrawati (1792) defined no line.
